knowledge:
- key_parameters: <exclude.regions=A data.frame or GenomicRanges object containing genomic regions (e.g., CNVs or blacklisted regions) to exclude from the analysis ;; exclude.overlap=The percentage overlap required with the regions listed in the data to trigger exclusion (default is 0.2, or 20%) ;; scale=Logical parameter in create.hic.table; set to FALSE if performing total sum scaling on the entire genome before loess normalization ;; span=The proportion of data used to build the loess model in hic_loess; if NA, automatic smoothing parameter selection runs ;; loess.criterion=The selection process for automatic span selection, either 'gcv' (generalized cross-validation) or 'aicc' (Akaike information criterion) ;; parallel=Logical parameter in hic_loess and hic_compare; set to TRUE to enable parallel processing via BiocParallel when a list of hic.tables is provided ;; A.min=The minimum average expression threshold in hic_compare used to filter out low-signal interactions before Z-score calculation (defaults to the 10th percentile if NA) ;; adjust.dist=Logical parameter in hic_compare to adjust for distance-dependent differences ;; p.method=The multiple testing correction method applied to p-values in hic_compare (e.g., 'fdr')>
- alternatives: <MA_norm=Performs MA normalization on a hic.table object instead of loess normalization ;; KRnorm=Performs Knight-Ruiz normalization on a full Hi-C matrix ;; SCN=Performs Sequential Component Normalization on a full Hi-C matrix>
- when_to_use: <Use this package when you have processed intrachromosomal Hi-C contact matrices from two or more experimental conditions and want to jointly normalize them to remove biases and identify statistically significant differential chromatin interactions.>
- pitfalls: <Do not use iced .matrix files from HiC-Pro; only use raw .matrix files because iced files have already undergone ICE normalization and are unsuitable for HiCcompare ;; HiCcompare is currently designed only for intrachromosomal (cis) interactions, not interchromosomal (trans) interactions ;; High-resolution matrices (e.g., 1KB to 50KB) are typically too sparse due to insufficient sequencing coverage and may not perform well ;; Low average expression interactions can lead to artificially large log2 fold changes from small raw differences; always filter them out using the A.min parameter to avoid false positives.>

workflows.name: standard_hic_comparison
workflows.intent: Jointly normalize and detect differential chromatin interactions between two Hi-C datasets for a single chromosome.
input: HMEC.chr22 (sparse upper triangular matrix file or R data frame)
NHEK.chr22 (sparse upper triangular matrix file or R data frame)
workflows.stages:
1. Load the sparse chromatin interaction matrices.
2. Create a hic.table object using create.hic.table.
3. Jointly normalize the datasets using hic_loess.
4. Evaluate filtering parameters using filter_params.
5. Detect differential interactions using hic_compare.
6. Convert the results to an InteractionSet object using make_InteractionSet.
workflows.code:
library(`HiCcompare`)
# load the data
data("HMEC.chr22")
data("NHEK.chr22")
head(HMEC.chr22)
# create the `hic.table` object
chr22.table <- create.hic.table(HMEC.chr22, NHEK.chr22, chr = 'chr22')
head(chr22.table)
# Jointly normalize data for a single chromosome
hic.table <- hic_loess(chr22.table, Plot = TRUE, Plot.smooth = FALSE)
knitr::kable(head(hic.table))
filter_params(hic.table)
hic.table <- hic_compare(hic.table, A.min = 15, adjust.dist = TRUE, p.method = 'fdr', Plot = TRUE)
knitr::kable(head(hic.table))
IntSet <- make_InteractionSet(hic.table)

workflows.name: genome_wide_parallel_comparison
workflows.intent: Perform genome-wide joint normalization and difference detection across multiple chromosomes using total sum scaling and parallel processing on a cluster.
input: dat1.1000000.pixels.tsv (genome-wide sparse interaction table for condition 1)
dat2.1000000.pixels.tsv (genome-wide sparse interaction table for condition 2)
workflows.stages:
1. Read and split the genome-wide interaction tables by chromosome.
2. Create a list of chromosome-specific hic.table objects with scale = FALSE.
3. Perform total sum scaling across all chromosomes using total_sum.
4. Register a parallel backend using BiocParallel.
5. Jointly normalize all chromosomes in parallel using hic_loess.
6. Detect differential interactions in parallel using hic_compare.
7. Combine results and filter by adjusted p-value.
workflows.code:
library(HiCcompare)
library(BiocParallel)

args = commandArgs(trailingOnly=TRUE)

dat1 <- read.table(args[1], header=FALSE, col.names=c("chr1", "start1", "end1", "chr2", "start2", "end2", "IF"))
dat2 <- read.table(args[2], header=FALSE, col.names=c("chr1", "start1", "end1", "chr2", "start2", "end2", "IF"))

dat1 <- dat1[dat1$chr1==dat1$chr2, ]
dat2 <- dat2[dat2$chr1==dat2$chr2, ]

dat1 <- split(dat1, dat1$chr1)
dat2 <- split(dat2, dat2$chr1)

hic.list <- mapply(create.hic.table, dat1, dat2, SIMPLIFY = FALSE, scale=FALSE)

hic.list <- total_sum(hic.list)

register(MulticoreParam(workers = 10), default = TRUE)

hic.list <- hic_loess(hic.list, Plot=TRUE, parallel=TRUE)
hic.list <- hic_compare(hic.list, A.min = NA, adjust.dist = TRUE, p.method = 'fdr', Plot = TRUE, parallel=TRUE)

hic.list <- do.call(rbind, hic.list)

hic.list <- hic.list[hic.list$p.adj<0.05,]

write.table(hic.list, args[3])

workflows.name: hic_simulation_and_evaluation
workflows.intent: Simulate two Hi-C matrices with added bias and true differences to evaluate the performance of difference detection.
input: None (this workflow generates simulated data based on user-defined parameters)
workflows.stages:
1. Define simulation parameters including matrix dimensions, number of changes, and indices of cells to alter.
2. Simulate matrices, apply loess normalization, and detect differences using hic_simulate.
3. (Alternative) Generate raw simulated matrices without downstream analysis using sim_matrix.
workflows.code:
number_of_unitdistances <- 100 # The dimensions of the square matrix to be simualted
number_of_changes       <- 250 # How many cells in the matrix will have changes
i.range <- sample(1:number_of_unitdistances, number_of_changes, replace = TRUE) # Indexes of cells to have controlled changes
j.range <- sample(1:number_of_unitdistances, number_of_changes, replace = TRUE) # Indexes of cells to have controlled changes

sim_results <- hic_simulate(nrow = number_of_unitdistances, medianIF = 50000, sdIF = 14000, powerlaw.alpha = 1.8, fold.change = 4, i.range = i.range, j.range = j.range, Plot = TRUE, alpha = 0.1)

names(sim_results)

sims <- sim_matrix(nrow = number_of_unitdistances, medianIF = 50000, sdIF = 14000, powerlaw.alpha = 1.8, fold.change = 4, 
                   i.range = i.range, j.range = j.range)
